apps.name: Arkive
apps.tagline: Scripture one verse at a time, with the Hebrew and Greek, history and maps beside it.
apps.about: Read a verse per page or by chapter, tap any word for the original language, and follow it through the whole Bible. Commentaries, dictionaries, a timeline and journey maps sit behind the text, and your notes and study threads sync through your own iCloud. For families, 47 illustrated Bible stories read aloud, and historical photographs from the Library of Congress open the chapters and places the engravings don't cover.
highlights: Three SwiftData stores in one container: bundled Bible text, a purgeable cache for online text, and CloudKit-synced user data with merge rules for records two devices create at once.
Full-text and grammar search over a prebuilt SQLite FTS5 index, including 440,000 original-language words searchable by Strong's number, tense and voice.
A licensed translation fetched live from the YouVersion API and transcoded from HTML into the app's own text format, so every reader feature works on it unchanged.
Read to Me: on-device speech with an IPA pronunciation lexicon for biblical names, a Live Activity, a sleep timer and Personal Voice support.
MapKit timelines and animated journey routes, plus a deep-zoom 1878 history chart drawn with CATiledLayer and tappable scenes.
Apple-hosted Background Assets with an ExtensionKit downloader, so 60 MB of story art and photographs download on demand or in the background instead of shipping in the app.
Python data pipelines that turn public-domain lexicons, dictionaries, commentaries, stories and photo archives into validated bundles, with license and rights checks built in.
Siri and Shortcuts, Spotlight, Handoff, hardware keyboard shortcuts and the iPad menu bar.

apps.name: Pyllar
apps.tagline: Run a lawn care business from one place: scheduling, dispatch, invoicing and the crew's day.
apps.about: A multi-tenant SaaS for lawn care and landscaping companies, built and run by my company, C&F Solutions LLC. Crews work from native iOS and Android apps, owners run the business from a web app, and customers pay and request work through their own portal.
highlights: Native iOS (Swift 6, SwiftUI) and Android (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose) apps kept at feature parity, with a Live Activity for the job in progress.
Next.js web app, customer portal and internal staff portal on a TypeScript Fastify API with PostgreSQL and Drizzle.
An AI assistant built on Claude that returns structured intents, which the API validates and permission-checks by role before acting.
Stripe billing and invoice payments, Typesense search, and role-based access control across owners, managers and technicians.
Dockerized deploys to staging and production through GitHub Actions.

apps.name: Tydé
apps.tagline: A calm cleaning planner built for ADHD brains: one room a day, and no guilt.
apps.about: Every task is sorted Easy, Medium or Deep, so a low-energy day still has a real session in it. Pick up to three must-dos, and spin the wheel when you can't decide where to start.
highlights: SwiftData with CloudKit sync for rooms, tasks, plans and history, with no account and no server.
A Home Screen widget that shows today's room and can spin for a task without opening the app, plus a Live Activity for the focus timer, sharing data through an App Group.
Siri and Shortcuts through App Intents: spin for a task or hear today's room hands-free.
Lottie animations for the moments that matter, and copy written to avoid streak-shaming or guilt.

apps.name: Whisper Court
apps.tagline: You are a Renaissance spymaster. Spread one rumor through the court.
apps.about: Gossips spread it, skeptics need two sources, and the loyal will expose you. Each turn you whisper, silence, forge or bribe before the rumor travels one more step, and every court can be won in a set number of turns.
highlights: A deterministic rules engine in its own Swift package, with no UI code, so every rule is unit-tested.
A solver that proves each level's best score; tests fail if a level's par isn't the true optimum or if its new mechanic isn't actually needed.
Swift 6 and SwiftUI, with Swift Testing and an XcodeGen project.

apps.name: Candidly
apps.tagline: Control your Mac from your iPhone or iPad, and keep an eye on it from any app.
apps.about: Candidly connects to the Screen Sharing that's already built into macOS, so there's nothing to install on the Mac. Use your phone as the trackpad and keyboard, float your Mac in Picture in Picture while you use other apps, get a notification when a build or export finishes, copy text straight off the screen, keep up to four Macs open, and wake a sleeping one with a tap. Your computers and their passwords follow you through iCloud. One price, no subscription.
highlights: The VNC (RFB) protocol written from scratch in Swift, including Apple's Screen Sharing extensions: Mac account sign-in over Diffie-Hellman and RSA, display selection, the shared-or-private session choice, the Mac clipboard and curtain mode. No third-party code.

Whole-session encryption with Apple's own Screen Sharing scheme (AES-128 records, on by default after Mac account sign-in), a lock in the viewer, and a per-computer setting that refuses unencrypted sessions.
A Metal renderer that uploads only the parts of the screen that changed, so a 5K Mac stays smooth on an iPhone, plus ZRLE, Zlib, Hextile and CopyRect decoders hardened against a misbehaving server.

Picture in Picture for a remote screen: frames scaled with vImage into an AVSampleBufferDisplayLayer, a session that stays live in the background while PiP is open, and a handover when you switch Macs or windows.
Watch Area: draw a box over the Mac's screen and get a notification when it changes or stops changing, using a luminance grid that ignores a blinking cursor but catches a slow progress bar.
Up to four Macs open at once with a switcher, and multiple windows on iPad, built on an app-wide session manager that pauses whatever isn't on screen.

Select Text with Live Text (VisionKit) on a full-resolution crop of what you're looking at, Wake-on-LAN with an on-demand check for Macs that aren't responding, Trackpad Only mode, and custom shortcut buttons on the key strip.

Touch and Trackpad modes with the full gesture set (multi-finger clicks and drags, two-finger scroll, pinch zoom at your fingers, edge and corner swipes, three-finger swipes for Mission Control and Spaces) and the Mac's real pointer drawn on the device.
Saved computers sync through iCloud with merge rules and deletion tombstones, passwords live in iCloud Keychain, and Macs on the network are found with Bonjour.

screens.alt: Your Mac, wherever you are. Full control from your iPhone. Nothing to install on the Mac.
Keep an eye on it from any app. Picture in Picture keeps your Mac live while you do something else.
Get a ping when it's done. Draw a box around any part of the screen. Candidly tells you when it changes or stops.
Every Mac you own, one tap apart. Keep up to four Macs open and switch in a tap.
Copy text right off the screen. Error messages, logs, links: select them and paste anywhere.
Wake a sleeping Mac with a tap. See which Macs are asleep, wake one, then connect.
Every key, plus your own shortcuts. ⌘, Esc, arrows, F-keys, and buttons for the combos you use most.
Just a trackpad, when you can see the Mac. Hide the picture and drive a Mac on your TV from the couch.
Pay once. No subscription. Encrypted sessions, Face ID, curtain mode, and Tailscale or your own VPN. No account.
